name: Saltwind apartment house
role: Continuous residential blocks behind the square
design: A BROAD MEDIUM-HEIGHT THREE-STOREY apartment house, approximately 10 m wide by 7 m deep. Rectangular mass with a LOW HIPPED deep-teal tiled roof and two squat brick chimney stacks, no attic storey or tower. Pale buttery plaster over a limestone ground floor, warm honey-oak window lintels and faded blue-green shutters; three regularly spaced window bays across the street facade, a single recessed central entry with a small practical stone hood. Use a few simple window boxes and pale linen curtains, not a mass of ivy. Continuous clear horizontal eaves make it read wider and calmer than a narrow gabled house. The rear has the same three levels with a quieter window rhythm, a ground utility door, a small covered shared laundry alcove and rain barrel. One end wall is almost plain, suitable for a close neighbour. Entire roof, rear wall and both end facades visible across the paired views.
